ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Diana draws a rectangle made up of twelve squares onto a piece of squared paper. Some of the squares are coloured in black. She writes the number of adjacent black squares into every white square. The diagram shows an example of such a rectangle. Now she does the same with a rectangle made up of 2018 squares. What is the biggest number that she can obtain as the sum of all numbers in the white squares?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure is a rectangle composed of 3 rows and 4 columns, a total of 12 small squares. Some squares are black, and numbers are written in the remaining white squares. For example, the white square in the second column of the middle row has 3 written in it; above it, to its right, and below it are all black squares, so the number indicates the number of black squares adjacent to that white square with a common edge; this also shows that only edge adjacency is counted, and diagonal adjacency is not counted. Then reason: Regard each small square as a vertex of a grid graph, and connect an edge between two small squares that have a common edge. The sum of the numbers in all white squares is exactly equal to the total number of adjacent edges between black squares and white squares. For an m×n rectangular grid, the total number of adjacent edges is horizontal edges m(n-1) plus vertical edges n(m-1), namely m(n-1)+n(m-1)=2mn-m-n. Since this kind of grid graph is a bipartite graph, using checkerboard coloring can make every adjacent edge connect one black square and one white square, so for fixed m,n the maximum total sum is the number of all adjacent edges 2mn-m-n. Now there are altogether 2018 squares, 2018=2×1009, and 1009 is a prime number, so the rectangle dimensions can only be 1×2018 or 2×1009 (not counting rotations). If it is 1×2018, the maximum value is 2017. If it is 2×1009, the maximum value is 2×2018-2-1009=4036-1011=3025. Therefore the maximum possible total sum is 3025.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: it is a 3 by 4 rectangle of squares, with black squares and white squares labeled by how many edge-sharing black neighbors they have; for example the white square labeled 3 touches three black squares up/down/right, confirming that only side-adjacency is counted. From the text, the new rectangle has exactly 2018 unit squares and may have any rectangular dimensions with integer side lengths. Model the rectangle as a grid graph whose vertices are squares and whose edges join side-adjacent squares. The sum of all numbers written in white squares equals the number of black-white adjacent edges. For an m by n grid, there are m(n-1)+n(m-1)=2mn-m-n adjacent pairs total. Since the grid graph is bipartite, a checkerboard coloring makes every adjacent pair black-white, so the maximum for fixed m,n is all edges, namely 2mn-m-n. Factor 2018=2*1009, so possible rectangles are 1 by 2018 or 2 by 1009. Their maxima are 2017 and 2*2018-2-1009=3025 respectively. Choose the larger, 3025.

再推理：把每个小方格看成网格图的一个顶点，两个有公共边的小方格之间连一条边。所有白格中数字的总和，正好等于黑格与白格之间相邻边的总数。对于一个 m×n 的长方形网格，总相邻边数为横向边 m(n-1) 加纵向边 n(m-1)，即 m(n-1)+n(m-1)=2mn-m-n。由于这种网格图是二分图，用棋盘式染色可以使每一条相邻边都连接一个黑格和一个白格，所以固定 m,n 时最大总和就是全部相邻边数 2mn-m-n。
